subject: Using a progress bar in Shiny with rstan

messages.author: 3ef7a01c7d912ca2
messages.subject: Using a progress bar in Shiny with rstan
parts:
MCMC processing with R-packages rstan can easily keep the computer busy for several minutes, and the only feedback is the output to the console, or, when redirected, to a log file.

This is a problem when `rstan` is running in the main thread of a Shiny app, because there is no callback that can refresh the progress counter.

I have made a first attempt in implementing a progress bar with stan running in a separate process. The shiny program monitors the log file with a reactiveFileReader, updates the progress bar and displays the diagnostic plot on completion.

https://github.com/dmenne/shiny_stan_progress

This is not a package, you have to download it to your computer, and run it locally. Running it via `runGithub()` fails to display the progress bar.

There seem to be some caching problems involved when the log file is written; the progress bar moves on the first run, but rarely on any further run.

Any ideas how to solve this would be appreciated.

Dieter

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Using a progress bar in Shiny with rstan
parts:
It seems to work fine for me on Mac. I wonder if this is a Windows-specific issue? Perhaps sink(log_file) opens the file with an exclusive lock?

How about instead of doing sink(log_file), you use capture.output({ ... }) to grab the string output, then write it to the log file using cat(file=log_file, output)?

(BTW, I'm really hoping to have first-class support for a similar mechanism in a future version of Shiny. We want to build really good child process support into a future version of httpuv, which would make this kind of thing much easier.)
